guide.title: Ostiense, Rome: San Paolo fuori le Mura, Centrale Montemartini and Garbatella
guide.intro: Ostiense is the tenth of Rome's quartieri, Q. X in the official series, with the toponymic code 210. It begins outside the Aurelian Walls at Porta San Paolo and runs south along via Ostiense to the Magliana viaduct, with the Tiber on its western side. Standing in it are the papal basilica of San Paolo fuori le Mura, which is the property of the Holy See on Italian soil; a branch of the Musei Capitolini installed in a municipal power station of 1912; a Roman burial ground in a public park; two catacombs; the steel frame of a gasholder built in the 1930s; and Garbatella, the housing quarter whose foundation stone was laid on 18 February 1920. It is a quartiere and not one of the twenty-two rioni.

sections.heading: What Ostiense is, and where it stops
sections.body:
A quartiere is a different kind of unit from a rione. Roma Capitale's own framing of the toponymic areas is that they «non hanno alcuna relazione con le aree urbanistiche ne amministrative» - they have no relation to the administrative or town-planning areas.

it.wikipedia's article on the quartiere gives its edges: to the north the rioni Testaccio and San Saba, separated by the Aurelian Walls from the Tiber to Porta San Paolo and from Porta San Paolo to Porta Ardeatina; to the east the quartiere Ardeatino, separated by via Cristoforo Colombo and via Laurentina; to the south the quartiere Europa, separated by viale dell'Atletica and the Magliana viaduct as far as the river; and to the west the quartiere Portuense, separated by the Tiber from the Magliana viaduct to the Ponte dell'Industria. Several things a visitor meets on the way in stand outside those edges: the Piramide di Caio Cestio and the stretch of Aurelian Walls at it are in Testaccio, and Porta San Paolo, the Museo della Via Ostiense and the Palazzo delle Poste are in San Saba. Fighting took place at Porta San Paolo in September 1943. Ponte dell'Industria and the railway Ponte San Paolo cross to Portuense.

Garbatella, which many travellers treat as a district of its own, is the zona urbanistica 11C, and it lies inside quartiere Q. X Ostiense. Its streets and squares include piazza Benedetto Brin, piazza Damiano Sauli, piazza Eugenio Biffi, piazza Bartolomeo Romano. The name has never been settled. The it.wikipedia article carries three accounts: an innkeeper, Carlotta or Maria, so obliging that travellers called her the Garbata Ostella, syncopated to Garbatella; the pleasantness of the place; and the a garbata method of training vines used on the tenuta dei 12 cancelli, held in the nineteenth century by Monsignor Alessandro Nicolai. A 2019 study by Giorgio Guidoni in Garbatella 100 proposes that the innkeeper was Clementina Eusebi, who ran an inn on via Ostiense between about 1835 and 1850, and that the name came from her mother's surname, Maddalena Garbata, mother and daughter being distinguished as Garbata and Garbatella. All four are accounts, not conclusions. The name of the new quarter was itself argued over until about 1930, with Concordia and Remuria proposed instead.

One old road runs through the middle of all this. Via delle Sette Chiese is the road pilgrims took from San Paolo fuori le Mura to San Sebastiano, at right angles to the Ardeatina and the Appia; from the sixteenth century it was part of the Giro delle Sette Chiese, and it is still walked on the pilgrimage to the Santuario del Divino Amore. The Chiesoletta, San Filippo Neri in Eurosia, the Garbatella model houses of lotto 24 and the entrance to the Commodilla catacomb all stand on it. The road runs well beyond the quartiere in both directions. Two more recent facts belong to the same streets: the quartiere article records that Muccassassina began near the former gasworks on via Ostiense in the 1990s, and that Ferzan Ozpetek used an address on via del Porto Fluviale for Le fate ignoranti in 2001.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Three stations serve the quartiere. Piramide, on metro line B, was designed by Marcello Piacentini; its entrance steps rise onto the piazzale di Porta San Paolo, and a subway opened in 1990 links it to Roma Ostiense, with a second entrance and hall on via delle Cave Ardeatine. Roma Ostiense is the railway station on piazzale dei Partigiani. Roma Porta San Paolo is the terminus of the Roma-Lido railway, which passed from ATAC to COTRAL and ASTRAL with effect from 1 July 2022; the Polo museale dei trasporti, at Via Bartolomeo Bossi 7, stands next to it in the old goods yard. The Ponte Settimia Spizzichino carries the Circonvallazione Ostiense over the railway and metro line B, beside Garbatella station and the former Mercati Generali.

After that, steer by addresses, because the quartiere is long. The basilica of San Paolo fuori le Mura is at Piazzale San Paolo 1, 00146, and the monastic garden is entered at the Spezieria, Via Ostiense 186. Centrale Montemartini is at Via Ostiense 106, 00154, opposite the former Mercati Generali. The Sepolcreto della via Ostiense is inside Parco Ildefonso Schuster on via Ostiense. The Catacomba di Commodilla is at Via delle Sette Chiese 42, 00145, and the Catacomba di Santa Tecla is on via Silvio d'Amico, which follows the line of the old via delle Statue. Casa del Jazz is at Viale di Porta Ardeatina 55, 00154. Eataly's Rome store is inside the former air terminal at Piazzale XII Ottobre 1492. Roma Tre's rectorate is at Via Ostiense 133, and the Teatro Palladium at Piazza Bartolomeo Romano 8, 00154.

Two bridges here carry traffic across the Tiber and both lie between Ostiense and the quartiere Portuense: Ponte Guglielmo Marconi, inaugurated on 26 February 1955, and the cycle-and-foot Ponte della Scienza Rita Levi-Montalcini, whose Ostiense landfall is at the Gazometro.

sections.heading: Tickets, hours and booking
sections.body:
The basilica's own site gives it as open every day from 07:00 to 18:30, with free entry. The sacristy is open 08:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 18:30, and confessions are heard 10:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 18:30. Weekday Masses are at 07:00, 10:00 and 17:00 with Vespers at 18:00; on Sundays and solemnities they are at 08:00, 10:00 conventual and 12:00, with Vespers at 17:00 and Mass at 18:00. The cloister with the picture gallery, the relics chapel and the archaeological area is ticketed separately: daily 08:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:30, 4.00 euro full and 3.00 euro reduced, with groups of more than ten at 3.00 euro a head and the group's guide free.

Centrale Montemartini opens Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 19:00, with last entry an hour before closing, and is closed on Mondays, 1 May and 25 December; from 24 to 31 December it opens 09:00 to 14:00, and on 1 January 2026 from 11:00 to 20:00. Admission is 11.00 euro full and 6.50 euro reduced; the seven-day Capitolini Card, valid for the Musei Capitolini and Centrale Montemartini together, is 15.50 euro full and 11.50 euro reduced.

The Sepolcreto della via Ostiense must be booked. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina gives booking on 060608, 09:00 to 19:00, with a maximum of 25 people per visit and a maximum of ten at a time in the courtyard of the Rupe sector; admission is 4.00 euro full and 3.00 euro reduced, free for residents of Rome and the metropolitan area on production of identification and for MIC card holders, and the area is accessible to disabled visitors. The Catacomba di Commodilla is visited by request only, on +39 064465610 or +39 064467601 or at protocollo@arcsacra.va. The monastic garden of the abbey is opened only for booked guided visits, in spring and in autumn, on 06 698 80 811 or giardino@abbaziasanpaolo.org.

No source states opening hours for the Polo museale dei trasporti, for the Cisterna della via Colombo or for the Eataly store in the former air terminal, and no source states opening arrangements for the Catacomba di Santa Tecla, so none are given here. Forte Ostiense is a working police facility and the Gazometro site is a working private industrial estate; neither is a visitor site.

faq.question: Is San Paolo fuori le Mura on Italian soil?
faq.answer: Yes. The basilica stands on Italian soil, about two kilometres outside the Aurelian Walls, in quartiere Q. X Ostiense, at Piazzale San Paolo 1. The basilica and its annexed buildings are the property of the Holy See under Article 13 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Article 15 provides that the property, «benche facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» - although forming part of the territory of the Italian State - enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law. Article 16 of the same treaty covers a different list of properties and does not apply here.

faq.question: Is Garbatella a separate district?
faq.answer: No. Garbatella is the zona urbanistica 11C, and it lies inside quartiere Q. X Ostiense, which is why it has no page of its own here. Its buildings are written with their own addresses: the foundation inscription of 18 February 1920 on piazza Benedetto Brin, the Alberghi Suburbani on piazza Eugenio Biffi, Innocenzo Sabbatini's Teatro Palladium on piazza Bartolomeo Romano, Angelo Brunetta's school on piazza Damiano Sauli, and the thirteen model houses of lotto 24 between via delle Sette Chiese, via De Jacobis and via Borri.

faq.question: Can you go inside the Gazometro?
faq.answer: No. The site is a working private industrial estate. The frame is seen from via del Commercio, from the Ponte della Scienza and from the Riva Ostiense. What stands there is the steel frame of the gasholder erected by Ansaldo of Genoa with Klonne of Dortmund between 1935 and 1937: 89.10 metres high, 63 metres across, for a volume of 200,000 cubic metres. The holder bell itself was removed after the plant stopped working, so only the frame is left.

faq.question: Which catacombs are here, and how do you visit them?
faq.answer: Two. The Catacomba di Commodilla, at Via delle Sette Chiese 42, 00145, is run by the Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra, and visits are by request only, on +39 064465610 or +39 064467601 or at protocollo@arcsacra.va. It holds the martyrs Felix and Adauctus, the painting known as the Madonna di Turtura and the cubiculum of Leo, an official of the Annona. The Catacomba di Santa Tecla is on via Silvio d'Amico; no source states opening arrangements, so none are given here.

faq.question: Where can you eat in Ostiense?
faq.answer: Six addresses, and no clubs. Porto Fluviale is at Via del Porto Fluviale 22; Al Biondo Tevere at Via Ostiense 178; Pasticceria Andreotti at Via Ostiense 54b; Romeow Cat Bistrot at Via Francesco Negri 15; Hopside, a beer house, at Via Francesco Negri 39/41; and Tre de Tutto at Via Giustino de Jacobis 19 in Garbatella. Caffe Letterario, at Via Ostiense 95, has a library, the Bibliocaffe, and Eataly's Rome store is inside the former air terminal at Piazzale XII Ottobre 1492. No source states opening hours for any of them, so none are given here.

faq.question: What is Centrale Montemartini?
faq.answer: A municipal thermoelectric station of 1912 that now holds Capitoline sculpture among its turbines and diesel engines, at Via Ostiense 106, 00154. It was inaugurated under mayor Ernesto Nathan, following the referendum of 20 September 1909 on municipalising public services, and was named in 1913 for Giovanni Montemartini, Nathan's technical assessor, who died during a council session. It was decommissioned in the mid-1960s. Sculpture was moved here in 1997 during the restoration of the Musei Capitolini, for the exhibition Le macchine e gli dei; the museum became permanent in 2001.

places.name: Basilica papale di San Paolo fuori le Mura
places.summary: The papal basilica built over the tomb of St Paul, about two kilometres outside the Aurelian Walls on via Ostiense. Its own site gives it as open every day from 07:00 to 18:30 with free entry; the sacristy 08:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 18:30; confessions 10:00 to 12:00 and 16:00 to 18:30; weekday Mass at 07:00, 10:00 and 17:00 with Vespers at 18:00, and on Sundays and solemnities Mass at 08:00, 10:00 conventual and 12:00, with Vespers at 17:00 and Mass at 18:00. The basilica and its annexed buildings are the property of the Holy See under Article 13 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Article 15 provides that the property, «benche facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» - although forming part of the territory of the Italian State - enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law.
places.history: Tradition gives the consecration as 18 November 324 under Silvester I, on a foundation by Constantine; the church was rebuilt from 391 under Theodosius, Arcadius and Valentinian II, and that building stood until the fire of 1823. Leo XII ordered the rebuilding in the encyclical Ad plurimas of 25 January 1825 and in a chirograph of 18 September 1825 requiring that «niuna innovazione dovra dunque introdursi nelle forme e proporzioni architettoniche». Pasquale Belli directed the work on a Valadier scheme and Luigi Poletti gave the church its present appearance; Gregory XVI dedicated the altar of the Confession on 5 October 1840 and Pius IX consecrated the whole basilica on 10 September 1854. It measures 131 by 65 metres and is 29.70 metres high, with five aisles and four rows of twenty monolithic Montorfano granite columns. The quadriportico was built between 1890 and 1928 by Giuseppe Sacconi and Guglielmo Calderini on Poletti's scheme, with a marble statue of St Paul by Giuseppe Obici and gates by Gino Benigni, competition 1913 and installed 1926; the earthquake of 30 October 2016 damaged it. The facade mosaics were made between 1854 and 1874 to cartoons by Filippo Agricola and Nicola Consoni. Antonio Maraini's central bronze door of 1931 measures 7.48 by 3.35 metres and Enrico Manfrini's Holy Door 3.71 by 1.82 metres. The right-hand door is the 11th-century bronze door of 54 panels. It was the main entrance until 1967 and since then has been the inner face of the Holy Door. Poletti's campanile was finished in 1860; six of its seven bells were cast in 1959 by the Marinelli foundry of Agnone and the highest dates from 1653. The great bell, 'Pierpaola', sounds G2, measures two metres across and weighs about 5,000 kg. Inside are 267 papal tondi with 25 medallions still empty, and 36 frescoes of the life of St Paul finished in 1860; more than 1,700 inscribed slabs have been recovered from the floor burials. The triumphal arch carries the mosaic given by Galla Placidia under Leo I; the apse mosaic was made under Honorius III between 1216 and 1227; Arnolfo di Cambio made the ciborium in 1285, and Pietro Vassalletto and Nicolo D'Angelo the paschal candelabrum in 1170. Of the four transept chapels, the Santissimo Sacramento by Carlo Maderno survived the 1823 fire, the San Lorenzo chapel holds Andrea Bregno's marble triptych of 1494, and the San Benedetto chapel uses twelve antique columns from Veii; the adjoining Sala del Martirologio keeps 12th and 13th-century fresco fragments. The great organ was built in 1857-58 by Enrico Priori from Serassi material, with 36 stops and 2,556 pipes; a second organ, probably by William George Trice in 1891, has 12 stops and 698 pipes. Two popes are buried here, Felix III and John XIII. Tsar Nicholas I gave the malachite for the transept altars, the Viceroy of Egypt the alabaster columns, and King Fuad I of Egypt the alabaster window slabs after the explosion at Forte Portuense in 1891 shattered the earlier glass. UNESCO's World Heritage property, inscribed in 1980, is titled Historic Centre of Rome, the Properties of the Holy See in that City Enjoying Extraterritorial Rights and San Paolo Fuori le Mura, and that title names this basilica.

places.name: Chiostro e Area Espositiva e Archeologica di San Paolo
places.summary: The ticketed part of the basilica complex: the 13th-century cloister, the Pinacoteca, the Cappella delle Reliquie, an exhibition gallery and the archaeological area. Open daily 08:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:30; 4.00 euro full and 3.00 euro reduced, with groups of more than ten at 3.00 euro a head and «la guida del gruppo entra gratis». The basilica and its annexed buildings are the property of the Holy See under Article 13 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Article 15 provides that the property, «benche facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» - although forming part of the territory of the Italian State - enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law.
places.history: The excavation of the archaeological area began in 2007 and lasted about two years, under the direction of the Musei Vaticani with the Pontificio Istituto di Archeologia Cristiana. The basilica's own account gives the site as «vasto circa mille metri quadrati» and describes an oratory dedicated to Santo Stefano among the structures found. The cloister holds fragments from the old basilica together with finds from the neighbouring burial ground on via Ostiense.

places.name: Abbazia benedettina di San Paolo fuori le Mura
places.summary: The Benedictine monastery annexed to the basilica on piazzale San Paolo. Its monks keep the liturgy and the votive lamp at the tomb, and the house holds a monastic library. The basilica and its annexed buildings are the property of the Holy See under Article 13 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Article 15 provides that the property, «benche facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» - although forming part of the territory of the Italian State - enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law.
places.history: The territorial abbacy was suppressed on 7 March 2005, and on 31 May 2005 Benedict XVI's motu proprio L'antica e venerabile Basilica placed an archpriest over the basilica with the abbot as his vicar for pastoral care. The archpriests have been Andrea Cordero Lanza di Montezemolo from 2005 to 2009, Francesco Monterisi from 2009 to 2012, and James Michael Harvey since 23 November 2012. Dom Donato Ogliari is abbot.

places.name: Giardino monastico e Spezieria dell'Abbazia di San Paolo
places.summary: The monastic garden is entered at the Spezieria, Via Ostiense 186. The abbey states that it is normally not accessible to the public and opens it only for booked guided visits in two seasons a year, spring and autumn, for small groups and for a participation fee. Booking is on 06 698 80 811 or giardino@abbaziasanpaolo.org. The garden contains an orto dei semplici growing the officinal plants used in the herbal preparations sold at the Spezieria.
places.history: The garden belongs to the Benedictine abbey annexed to the basilica. The basilica and its annexed buildings are the property of the Holy See under Article 13 of the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Article 15 provides that the property, «benche facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» - although forming part of the territory of the Italian State - enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the seats of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law.

places.name: Sepolcreto della via Ostiense
places.summary: A Roman burial ground along the via Ostiense, inside Parco Ildefonso Schuster, kept by the Sovrintendenza Capitolina under its official name Sepolcreto della via Ostiense. Booking is obligatory on 060608, 09:00 to 19:00, with a maximum of 25 people per visit; admission is 4.00 euro full and 3.00 euro reduced, free for residents of Rome and the metropolitan area on production of identification and for MIC card holders, and a guided tour is not included. The Sovrintendenza states that the area is accessible to disabled visitors. The sector by the Rupe di San Paolo opened to the public on Wednesday 8 July 2026, 18:00 to 19:30, last entry 19:00; it holds nine burials, seen from the street front and around an internal courtyard where no more than ten people are admitted at a time, and a visit to the Sepolcreto now takes in both as one hour-long route.
places.history: The tombs were in continuous use from the 1st century BC to the 4th century AD, and the burials show the change from cremation to inhumation, and the tombs include quadrangular columbaria. Finds were recorded from the 1700s, with discoveries in 1859 and 1872 in the vigna Villani at the corner of via Ostiense and via delle Sette Chiese; a collector trench dug in 1897 and 1898 destroyed many burials but produced a great deal of epigraphy; the widening of via Ostiense in 1917 and 1918 documented the surviving sector, and a further widening in 1933 exposed the tombs now visible. The 1917-18 sector was roofed, restored and annexed to the green space of Parco Schuster for the Great Jubilee of 2000. The Rupe sector's display includes full-size reproductions of three frescoed lunettes, with new lighting and interpretive panels.

places.name: Catacomba di Commodilla
places.address: Via delle Sette Chiese 42, 00145 Roma RM
places.summary: A catacomb on via delle Sette Chiese, run by the Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra, with its entrance in the Parco di Commodilla. Visits are by request only, on +39 064465610 or +39 064467601 or at protocollo@arcsacra.va.
places.history: The name probably comes from the Roman matron who gave the land. The catacomb holds Felix and Adauctus, martyred under Diocletian in the early 4th century, in an underground basilica arranged under Damasus and Siricius and better defined under John I. Its paintings include the Madonna di Turtura, showing the Virgin enthroned between the two martyrs with the elderly woman who was buried there, a St Luke, a Traditio clavium, and the cubiculum of Leo, an official of the Annona. it.wikipedia records three levels, the middle one cut in an old pozzolana quarry, burials ending after the 4th century, devotional use in the 5th and 6th, coins of Gregory IV found on the site, and Leo IV's gift of the martyrs' relics to the wife of the Emperor Lothair. Antonio Bosio rediscovered the catacomb in 1595 and Giovanni Battista de Rossi identified it as Commodilla in the 19th century. Some burials are of the a pozzo type, shafts with up to twenty stacked loculi.

places.name: Catacomba di Santa Tecla
places.summary: A small catacomb on via Silvio d'Amico, which follows the line of the old via delle Statue. No source states opening arrangements, so none are given here.
places.history: A 4th-century underground basilica stands over a 3rd-century cemetery, whose three ambulacra are laid out as an isosceles triangle with 22 burial chambers. Who Tecla was is unresolved: Paul Styger argued for Thecla of Iconium, while Umberto Maria Fasola, who excavated the site in the later 20th century, argued for a Roman woman martyred under Diocletian.

places.name: Cisterna della via Colombo
places.summary: A Roman cistern on via Cristoforo Colombo, kept by the Sovrintendenza Capitolina. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: It was found in 1940 under a farmhouse demolished for the cuttings of the via Imperiale, now via Cristoforo Colombo; clearance was finished in 1969 and the structure was conserved and presented in 1991 and 1992. The cistern is circular, of the early 2nd century AD, built in opus reticulatum: a trapezoidal vestibule leads to a vaulted annular corridor divided into ten intercommunicating bays, then to a second undivided concentric corridor and a domed central chamber almost three metres across, the whole lined in signino.

places.name: Forte Ostiense
places.summary: A fort at the fourth kilometre of via Ostiense, from which it takes its name. Its own article places it in quartiere Q. X Ostiense, in the territory of Municipio Roma IX. It is now a working Polizia di Stato facility, housing the Centro Psicotecnico and the Servizio Tecnico Logistico, and it is not a visitor site.
places.history: It is one of the fifteen forts built round Rome between 1877 and 1891; work began in 1882 and finished in 1884, on a site of 8.8 hectares. On 10 September 1943 some eight hundred Grenadiers held out here against German paratroopers who had come up through the EUR; Don Pietro Occelli, director of the Istituto Gaetano Giardino next door, raised a white sheet to surrender the fort. Suor Teresina di Sant'Anna, born Cesarina D'Angelo, died on 8 May 1944 of injuries received from a German soldier in the fort's chapel.

places.name: Musei Capitolini Centrale Montemartini
places.summary: A branch of the Musei Capitolini in a municipal power station, where Roman sculpture stands among turbines, diesel engines and a steam boiler. Open Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 19:00, last entry an hour before closing, closed on Mondays, 1 May and 25 December; from 24 to 31 December it opens 09:00 to 14:00, and on 1 January 2026 from 11:00 to 20:00. Admission is 11.00 euro full and 6.50 euro reduced, with a seven-day Capitolini Card covering the Musei Capitolini and this museum at 15.50 euro full and 11.50 euro reduced. Among the works shown are the pediment statues of the temple of Apollo Sosianus, the colossal acrolith of Fortuna from Largo Argentina, the muse Polimnia, the seated girl, the portrait of Cleopatra, the Marsyas and the hunting mosaic from Santa Bibiana.
places.history: The thermoelectric station was inaugurated in 1912 under mayor Ernesto Nathan, following the referendum of 20 September 1909 on municipalising public services, which also created the AEM, today's Acea. In 1913 the plant was named for Giovanni Montemartini, Nathan's technical assessor, who died during a council session. It was sited between via Ostiense and the Tiber for water, rail and road, and beyond the customs boundary, so that its fuel paid no duty; steam turbines carried the base load and diesel engines the peaks. It was decommissioned in the mid-1960s, and Acea converted the Sala Macchine and the newer boiler hall into an art centre in the late 1980s. Capitoline sculpture was moved here in 1997 during the restoration of the Musei Capitolini, for the exhibition Le macchine e gli dei in October 1997; the museum became permanent in 2001, and in November 2016 a new room opened for the three carriages of the train of Pius IX, of 1858. The Sala Macchine keeps its Liberty-style fittings.

places.name: Gazometro di Roma
places.summary: The steel frame of a gasholder on via del Commercio, and the landmark of the industrial stretch of the quartiere. The site is a working private industrial estate. The frame is seen from via del Commercio, from the Ponte della Scienza and from the Riva Ostiense.
places.history: The gasworks and the first holders were designed in 1909 for the gas plant Ernesto Nathan wanted for the city. Samuel Cuttler & Sons of London built three smaller holders between 1910 and 1912, two of 25,000 cubic metres and one of 60,000. The great frame was erected by Ansaldo of Genoa with Klonne of Dortmund between 1935 and 1937 for the Societa Anglo-Romana per l'Illuminazione di Roma col Gas: 89.10 metres high, 63 metres in diameter, for a volume of 200,000 cubic metres, on 1,551 piles totalling 36 kilometres. After the plant stopped working the holder bell was removed and only the frame was left standing; of the three smaller holders, one became a gas pressure-reduction plant, one a technical building with a boiler house and stores, and one a multi-storey car park. Eni has owned the site, of more than twelve hectares, since 1967, through Italgas and Snam. The Luxometro lighting work dates from 2006; Eni's Joule school opened in 2020, the ZERO cleantech accelerator from 2021 and the Eni 2050 Lab from 2022, and ROAD, the Rome Advanced District, was inaugurated on 17 May 2023 by Eni, Acea, Autostrade per l'Italia, Bridgestone, Cisco, Gruppo FS and Nextchem. Maker Faire Rome was held here in 2021 and 2022.

places.name: Ex Mercati Generali
places.summary: The city's former general markets, on via Ostiense opposite Centrale Montemartini. They are closed, and the whole ex-markets area has been the subject of a long-running redevelopment.
places.history: The markets were designed by Francesco La Grassa and Emilio Saffi. Two different construction dates circulate in the same source and neither is given here.

places.name: Edificio d'ingresso ai Magazzini del Consorzio Agrario
places.address: Via del Porto Fluviale, Roma RM
places.summary: The entrance building to the warehouses of the Consorzio Agrario, on via del Porto Fluviale.
places.history: it.wikipedia's article on the quartiere dates it to 1925.

places.name: Ex caserma dell'Aeronautica, Via del Porto Fluviale 10
places.address: Via del Porto Fluviale 10, Roma RM
places.summary: A former air force barracks at Via del Porto Fluviale 10, occupied as the CSOA Fronte del Porto and carrying two entire painted facades by the street artist Blu, begun in 2013. No source states whether the building can be visited, so nothing is given here.
places.history: it.wikipedia's article on the quartiere lists the building under military architecture, and its article on Blu records the painting of two whole facades of an occupied building on via del Porto Fluviale, in the Ostiense quartiere, from 2013.

places.name: Stazione di Roma Ostiense
places.summary: The railway station on piazzale dei Partigiani, faced entirely in travertine, with a pillared portico, a 1940 relief of Bellerophon and Pegasus by Francesco Nagni on the right and a fountain with sea horses of 1957 on the left. Its floors carry black-and-white mosaics on Roman themes, from Aeneas leaving Carthage to St Peter's, designed by Giulio Rosso and Maria Immacolata Zaffuto.
places.history: A stop opened here on 1 May 1911 and was raised to a station on 21 October 1922. For Hitler's visit of 6 May 1938 a temporary monumental station was thrown up in 45 days, in Innocenti tubing faced with wood and stucco imitating travertine, to designs by Roberto Narducci; the permanent building, by the same designer, was built for the Exposition planned for 1942 and inaugurated on 28 October 1940. The avenue to Porta San Paolo and the forecourt were named via A. Hitler and piazzale A. Hitler for that visit, and are now viale delle Cave Ardeatine and piazzale dei Partigiani. Narducci's circular jet fountain on the forecourt was removed for the 1990 works and never restored; it appears at the end of Carlo Verdone's Un sacco bello.

places.name: Stazione di Roma Porta San Paolo
places.summary: The Rome terminus of the Roma-Lido railway, with a wide booking hall decorated with marine-themed frescoes by Giulio Rosso. Its own article places it in the quartiere Ostiense, in the territory of Municipio VIII. The Polo museale dei trasporti stands next to it, in the old goods yard, at Via Bartolomeo Bossi 7.
places.history: Work began in 1919 to designs by Marcello Piacentini, as the twin of his terminus at Marina di Ostia, and the station was inaugurated on 10 August 1924 with the first train to the Lido. It came through the war undamaged. It was modernised from 9 September 1989 to 1996, with the terminus falling back to EUR Magliana while the work was done.

places.name: Piramide (stazione della linea B)
places.address: Piazzale di Porta San Paolo, Roma RM
places.summary: A station on metro line B designed by Marcello Piacentini, of plain geometry roofed in white travertine slabs, with its entrance steps rising onto the piazzale di Porta San Paolo. Its platforms sit in an open cutting. A chapel dedicated to San Filippo Neri stands on the Rebibbia and Jonio platform.
places.history: Rolling stock of the Roma-Lido was sheltered in the unfinished station during the bombing of 1943. The station was refurbished in 1989, and in 1990 a subway to Roma Ostiense opened, with a second entrance and hall on via delle Cave Ardeatine.

places.name: Polo museale dei trasporti
places.summary: A transport museum in the old goods yard of the Roma-Lido terminus, partly open-air with restored rolling stock and partly indoors with models, instruments and the model of the stazione di Osilo. The museum was closed to the public from 2020, first under COVID-19 measures and then for maintenance pending funding from the Regione Lazio and the transfer of the Roma-Lido from ATAC to COTRAL and ASTRAL, effective 1 July 2022. It reopened on 14 October 2022. No source states its current opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Met.Ro. opened the museum on 18 September 2004, on an idea of the engineer Angelo Curci, during Rome's second notte bianca. Its stock was built between 1907 and 1945 and includes the Breda-AEG locomotive of 1915, STEFER no. 01, the Carminati & Toselli-TIBB of 1922, STEFER no. 05, the Stanga-TIBB ECD railcar of 1931, SRFN no. 21, and STFER tram no. 404 of 1941.

places.name: Ex Air Terminal Ostiense and Eataly Roma Ostiense
places.summary: A building put up as an air terminal with an attached shopping centre for the 1990 World Cup, on the far side of Stazione Ostiense, and now the home of Eataly's Rome store, which the company's own store directory lists as Roma Ostiense. No source states the store's opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: it.wikipedia's article on Garbatella records the air terminal with its shopping centre and camper area built for Italia '90 beyond the station, and that Eataly opened its Rome premises inside the Air Terminal in 2012.

places.name: Ponte Settimia Spizzichino
places.summary: A road bridge that crosses the railway and metro line B, beside Garbatella station and the former Mercati Generali, carrying the Circonvallazione Ostiense. It is a steel space-frame tied arch on three supports, carrying a double deck on steel cables: 160 metres overall, with a central suspended span of 126 metres and a rise of 42 metres, two carriageways of 16.5 metres with three lanes each and a 1.5-metre cycle lane in the central strip.
places.history: The executive design was by Solidus s.r.l., with Francesco Del Tosto, and the bridge was built by Cimolai SpA, with lighting by Francesco Bianchi, over three years on site; it was inaugurated on 20 June 2012 at a cost of about 15.4 million euro. It was named on the proposal of the giunta of Municipio VIII for Settimia Spizzichino, who survived the round-up of the Roman Ghetto on 16 October 1943 and deportation to Auschwitz.

places.name: Ponte Guglielmo Marconi
places.summary: A road bridge over the Tiber, lying between the quartieri Ostiense and Portuense. It is built on Gerber beams, runs about 235 metres, has a cross section of 32 metres with four lanes each way, and carries travertine parapets.
places.history: It was planned from the early 1930s and begun in 1937; work stopped during the war, resumed in 1953, and the bridge was inaugurated on 26 February 1955. It was restored in 1975.

places.name: Ponte della Scienza Rita Levi-Montalcini
places.summary: A cycle and pedestrian bridge over the Tiber, lying between the quartieri Portuense and Ostiense; its Ostiense landfall is at the Gazometro. It is 147 metres long overall, with a span of 90 metres.
places.history: An international competition was won in 2000 by APsT Architettura, with Gianluca Andreoletti, Maximiliano Pintore and Stefano Tonucci, and structures by Giorgio Monti and EDIN. Building began in 2008, by Maeg Costruzioni. The bridge opened briefly on 9 February 2013, opened to traffic on 29 May 2014 and was inaugurated on 8 July 2014, when the mayor named it for Rita Levi-Montalcini.

places.name: Piazza Benedetto Brin
places.summary: The square where Garbatella was founded. King Victor Emmanuel III laid the first stone here on 18 February 1920, Ash Wednesday, with Adolfo Apolloni as mayor. The lots around the square date from the foundation of 1920.
places.history: The inscription walled into the central building of the square reads: «Per la mano augusta di S.M. il Re Vittorio Emanuele III / l'Ente autonomo per lo sviluppo marittimo e industriale / e l'Istituto delle Case popolari di Roma / con la collaborazione delle Cooperative di lavoro / ad offrire quieta e sana stanza agli artefici del rinascimento economico della Capitale / questo aprico quartiere fondato oggi XVIII Febbraio MCMXX.»

places.name: Piazza Damiano Sauli
places.summary: The square at the centre of Garbatella, defined by the Cesare Battisti school, the church of San Francesco Saverio and a block of housing and shops on the north side, whose three central archways lead through to piazza Nicola Longobardi.
places.history: The square was rebuilt in the 1990s under Rome's 100 Piazze programme.

places.name: Scuola Cesare Battisti
places.summary: A school building of 1931 by Angelo Brunetta, raised by a storey in 1937: two C-shaped wings, originally of three storeys and now four over a basement, joined by a two-storey block crowned with a tower, with a double-height gymnasium, reinforced-concrete piers and floors, large glazing and an iron crown. It is a working school. No source states whether it can be visited, so nothing is given here.
places.history: It was originally named for the fascist gerarca Michele Bianchi, at Mussolini's wish. It has been used as a location in Nanni Moretti's Bianca and in the television series I Cesaroni.

places.name: Chiesa di San Francesco Saverio alla Garbatella
places.summary: Garbatella's parish church on piazza Damiano Sauli, by Alberto Calza Bini, with a brick and travertine facade, a central portal under a large lunette window, the arms of Pius XI above and a high dome. Inside are three aisles on Ionic columns and a transept, an apse canvas of the saint preaching, a Madonna del Divino Amore succouring Rome after the 1943 bombing, a Christ in glory with angels, and a bronze Crucifixion and Madonna flanking the entrance.
places.history: ArchiDiAP dates the building to 1931-1933, and Pius XI erected the parish on 1 May 1933 by the constitution Quo omnes sacrorum. John Paul II came to the parish on 3 December 1978 and told the congregation: «E una grande gioia per me poter visitare come prima parrocchia romana proprio la vostra … negli anni dell'immediato dopoguerra, come studente a Roma, mi recavo quasi ogni domenica proprio alla Garbatella, per aiutare nel servizio pastorale.»

places.name: Teatro Palladium
places.summary: A theatre on piazza Bartolomeo Romano in Garbatella, owned and run by the Universita Roma Tre through the Fondazione Roma Tre Teatro Palladium, programming theatre, cinema, music and dance. Its telephone number is +39 06 57332772. The auditorium is horseshoe-shaped and has no pit. On the same square stands the Bagni Pubblici, also by Sabbatini.
places.history: Innocenzo Sabbatini designed the building, put up in 1927-28 as the Cinema Teatro Garbatella, in lot 12, building 6, of the Istituto per le Case Popolari, with private flats on six floors above the auditorium.

places.name: Albergo Rosso and the Alberghi Suburbani
places.summary: The Albergo Rosso on piazza Eugenio Biffi, by Innocenzo Sabbatini, 1927-1928, identified by its clock tower, its render colour and a slight shift in its setting-out from the other three Alberghi.
places.history: Four Alberghi Suburbani - Rosso, Bianco, Giallo and Beige - were built from 1927 for the Istituto Case Popolari under Alberto Calza Bini, who called them «Alberghi di transito», for families evicted by the sventramenti of the late 1920s. They combined temporary housing with collective services: a canteen, a creche and a school, a chapel, laundries and ironing rooms, kitchens, shared washrooms, day rooms, outdoor play space and stores. Sabbatini resigned from the ICP on 7 March 1929 over changes made during construction.

places.name: Lotto 24, the casette modello
places.address: Via delle Sette Chiese, Roma RM
places.summary: Thirteen villini between via delle Sette Chiese, via De Jacobis and via Borri, built for the XII International Congress of Housing and Town Planning of 1929, with marble plaques at the entrances naming the architects.
places.history: The competition for the lot was won by the corner building at via delle Sette Chiese and via Borri, by Mario De Renzi.

places.name: Fontana della Carlotta and the Scala degli Innamorati
places.address: Piazza Ricoldo da Montecroce, Roma RM
places.summary: A fountain on piazza Ricoldo da Montecroce with the flight of steps beside it, known as the Scala degli Innamorati.
places.history: The Carlotta of the name is the innkeeper of one of the accounts given for the name Garbatella, in which travellers called her the Garbata Ostella; it is one account among several and is not settled.

places.name: Chiesa dei Santi Isidoro e Eurosia
places.address: Via delle Sette Chiese, Roma RM
places.summary: A small church on via delle Sette Chiese, known as la Chiesoletta, on the pilgrimage route between San Paolo and San Sebastiano. The entrance pronaos is attributed to Giuseppe Valadier, and the portico holds three plaster relief bozzetti held to be by Antonio Canova: a Virgin with the Child and St John the Baptist, The Saviour receiving the children, and St John the Baptist baptising Christ. Inside there is a single nave with a central altar in polychrome marble, four side windows and a cantoria.
places.history: An external plaque records that it was built in 1818 by Monsignor Nicola Maria Nicolai, whose family held the neighbouring tenuta dei 12 cancelli; the dedicatory inscription of 1818 survives. The church fell into ruin in the 19th century and was bought and restored by the Oratorian priest Generoso Calenzio. It is now annexed to the parish of San Filippo Neri in Eurosia, under the Oratorian Confederation.

places.name: Chiesa di San Filippo Neri in Eurosia
places.address: Via delle Sette Chiese, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church on via delle Sette Chiese, brick outside with a portico and a campanile at the side. On the trabeation is the Gospel line «Venite a me voi tutti che siete affaticati ed oppressi ed io vi ristorero», and at the top of the facade «D.O.M. in honorem S. Philippi Nerii A.D. MCMLII». Inside are three aisles on stone columns and a fibreglass statue of the saint flanked by portraits of Cesare Baronio and John Henry Newman; a mural of Filippo Neri was painted on the flank in 1996.
places.history: It was built between 1952 and 1955 to designs by Pier Luigi Maruffi, at the suggestion of Giovanni Battista Montini, with the benefactors Tommaso and Irene Bradley. Cardinal Vicar Clemente Micara erected the parish on 20 December 1952 by the decree Mirabili sollicitudine, and it is entrusted to and owned by the Oratorian Congregation. Paul VI created the cardinalatial title on 7 June 1967, visited on 19 February 1967, and John Paul II came on 23 February 1982.

places.name: Palazzo della Regione Lazio
places.summary: A rationalist office complex on via Cristoforo Colombo, with entrances on piazza Odorico da Pordenone, in the Garbatella zona urbanistica of quartiere Q. X Ostiense. It has three blocks: palazzina A on the Colombo, holding the president's offices; palazzina B in the middle, the tallest, holding the regional directorates; and palazzina C, for the service companies. It is a working seat of regional government. No source states whether it can be visited, so nothing is given here.
places.history: It was built as the national headquarters of INAM; after that body was wound up the building passed in 1980 to the Lazio regional giunta, and the Regione Lazio bought it in 2009. It served as the Megaditta in Fantozzi in 1975, which is why Romans call it the Palazzo di Fantozzi.

places.name: Chiesa di San Benedetto
places.summary: A brick parish church of two orders on via del Gazometro, served by the Society of the Divine Word. An atrium on two piers carries the motto «Obsculta o fili praecepta magistri: ora et labora», with an oval window above bearing a cross, a fish, a chi-rho, a dove and a crozier, and the arms of Pius XII at the top. The interior has a single nave with a right-hand aisle and four chapels on the left.
places.history: Pius X decided in 1912 to build a church by the gasworks but died before the work began; Benedict XV started it, and the dedication to St Benedict remembers him. A hut was fitted out as a church in 1916, and only piers and roof stood at Benedict XV's death; the work was finished under Pius XI, who erected the parish on 3 June 1926 by the constitution Nostri pastoralis officii. The chapels hold a Sacred Heart mosaic by Armando Baldinelli, a Madonna and Child by Silvio Consadori of 1951, a St Joseph with the adolescent Christ by Luigi Filocamo of 1953, a San Benedetto by Ferruccio Ferrazzi at the high altar and a terracotta Via Crucis by Antonio Giuseppe Santagata. Plaques record John Paul II's visit of 14 February 1988 and the elevation to a cardinalatial deaconry on 28 June 1988.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Galla
places.summary: A parish church of 1940 by Tullio Rossi on the Circonvallazione Ostiense, with a travertine colonnade round the sagrato, a brick facade a salienti, the arms of Pius XII over the window and a campanile with three bells in E3 cast in 1940 by Cobalchini of Padua. Inside are three aisles on red marble columns, a trussed timber ceiling, fourteen clear windows and a semicircular apse.
places.history: Cardinal Vicar Francesco Marchetti Selvaggiani erected the parish on 13 December 1940 by the decree Templum in honorem, and Cardinal Ugo Poletti consecrated the church on 15 December 1990, the parish's fiftieth anniversary; Paul VI visited on 13 March 1966 and John Paul II on 25 January 1981. The church keeps works from the old church of Santa Galla, demolished in 1935 for the widening of via del Teatro Marcello. Its altar is a white marble funerary altar of full Flavian date, reused as a Christian reliquary in the 11th century; it came from Santa Maria in Portico, demolished in 1932, stood briefly in San Giorgio in Velabro, and has been here since 20 September 1988. Two incised inscriptions on it record Gregory VII's consecration of Santa Maria in Portico and the altar's own consecration on 8 July 1073, listing relics of the True Cross and of the sponge, of the cross of St Andrew and parts of his bones, and of 21 other martyrs, six of them women; its four carved fronts show a stork pecking a bee, a sparrow with a shoot, a pelican, and a laurel tree with birds. The organ by Bartolomeo Formentelli was developed to 2003 from a core of 1967: fully mechanical, 94 stops and more than 5,000 pipes, with four manuals of 58 notes and a pedalboard of 30.

places.name: Basilica di Santa Maria Regina degli Apostoli alla Montagnola
places.summary: A church on via Antonino Pio run by the Societa San Paolo, on a central plan under a large dome, Roman-Baroque in inspiration, with Marian frescoes by Antonio Giuseppe Santagata. It carries the title of minor basilica, conferred in 1984.
places.history: Don Giacomo Alberione, founder of the Famiglia Paolina, had wanted a shrine to Mary Queen of Apostles, and the decision to build was taken in 1943 after a bombing on the site caused no casualties. The church was built after the war to a design by Leone Favini and finished in 1954. It has held a cardinalatial title since 1965 and became a parish in 1976 by will of Paul VI. It holds the remains of Don Alberione, of Tecla Merlo and of Giuseppe Timoteo Giaccardo, and the funeral of the exorcist Gabriele Amorth was held here on 19 September 2016.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Marcella
places.address: Piazza Nicoloso da Recco, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church on piazza Nicoloso da Recco by Leonardo Del Bufalo, on a hexagonal plan with a matroneum along the side walls and the counter-facade, and a tall reinforced-concrete campanile alongside.
places.history: Cardinal Vicar Clemente Micara instituted the parish on 13 May 1958 by the decree Qua celeritate. The church holds two altarpieces by the Abruzzese painter Marcello Ercole, exhibited at the IX Quadriennale in 1965, a counter-facade fresco by Dilvo Lotti, and a Mascioni organ, opus 962, of 1973.

places.name: Casa del Jazz (Villa Osio)
places.address: Viale di Porta Ardeatina 55, 00154 Roma RM
places.summary: A concert venue in a confiscated villa and its park, run by the Fondazione Musica per Roma; telephone 06 80241281. The auditorium seats about 150 and is named the Sala concerti Armando Trovajoli; the house also holds rehearsal and recording rooms, a guest house for visiting musicians and a restaurant, and Amerigo Bartoli's fresco of a view of Piazza Navona is in the ground-floor former dining room. Villa Osio covers 2,500 square metres in a park of 25,240. The box office opens on performance days from 19:00 until 40 minutes after the start, and tickets are sold through TicketOne.
places.history: The villa was built between 1936 and 1939 on the ruins of a 17th-century casale for Arturo Osio, co-founder of the Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, by the engineer Cesare Pascoletti, with the park laid out by Pietro Porcinai. In the 1980s Enrico Nicoletti, of the Banda della Magliana, bought it from the Vicariate and made heavy unauthorised alterations. It was seized on 14 November 1996, definitively confiscated on 20 February 2001, and assigned to the Comune di Roma on 26 September 2001 under law 109/1996; Casa del Jazz opened in April 2005. A stele at the park gate, made with Libera, carries 683 names of victims of the mafia between 1893 and 2005.

places.name: Universita degli Studi Roma Tre, Ostiense campus
places.summary: The university's premises along via Ostiense and the streets behind it: the rectorate at Via Ostiense 133, the student registry at 123 and the ex Tommaseo building at 139, home of the DAMS; Largo San Leonardo Murialdo and Via della Vasca Navale 79 and 84 for science and engineering; Via Gabriello Chiabrera 199; and Via Silvio D'Amico 77. The university also owns and runs the Teatro Palladium in Garbatella.
places.history: The university has had premises in the quartiere since 1992. Its recent building recoveries include the ex Vasca Navale, and it.wikipedia's article on Garbatella records that one of its seats occupies the old glassworks at the foot of the quarter.

places.name: Caffe Letterario
places.summary: A cafe at Via Ostiense 95 with a library, the Bibliocaffe, which it.wikipedia's article on the quartiere lists among the libraries of Ostiense.

places.name: Parco Ildefonso Schuster
places.summary: A public park on via Ostiense, which contains the Sepolcreto della via Ostiense and the Monumento ai Caduti di Nassiriya.
places.history: The monument was inaugurated on 30 March 2008 for the victims of the attack of 12 November 2003 on the Italian base at Nasiriyah, and is the work of the sculptor Giuseppe Spagnulo. The Roman burial ground in the park was roofed, restored and annexed to the park's green space for the Great Jubilee of 2000.

places.name: Quartiere INA-Casa di Valco San Paolo
places.address: Via Valco di San Paolo, Roma RM
places.summary: A housing quarter between via Valco di San Paolo, via Corinto, via Efeso and via Filomene, with four star-plan towers of eight storeys, three flats to a floor and 24 flats each. The scheme covers 8,000 square metres and holds 440 dwellings and 2,600 rooms.
places.history: It was built in 1949 and 1950 for the INA-Casa and the IACP, by Mario De Renzi, Saverio Muratori, Eugenio Montuori, Mario Paniconi, Giulio Pediconi and Fernando Puccioni.

places.name: Porto Fluviale
places.address: Via del Porto Fluviale 22, Roma RM
places.summary: A restaurant at Via del Porto Fluviale 22. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Al Biondo Tevere
places.summary: A restaurant at Via Ostiense 178. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Pasticceria Andreotti
places.summary: A pastry shop and cafe at Via Ostiense 54b. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Romeow Cat Bistrot
places.summary: A cat bistrot at Via Francesco Negri 15. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Hopside
places.summary: A beer house at Via Francesco Negri 39/41, on the same street as Romeow Cat Bistrot. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Tre de Tutto
places.address: Via Giustino de Jacobis 19, Roma RM
places.summary: A pub at Via Giustino de Jacobis 19, in Garbatella, on one of the three streets that bound the model houses of lotto 24. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

entries.name: Basilica papale di San Paolo fuori le Mura
entries.note: The basilica over the tomb of St Paul, rebuilt after the fire of 1823 and consecrated by Pius IX on 10 September 1854; open daily 07:00 to 18:30, entry free.

entries.name: Chiostro e Area Espositiva e Archeologica di San Paolo
entries.note: The 13th-century cloister with the picture gallery, the relics chapel and the excavated area of about a thousand square metres, open daily 08:00 to 18:00 at 4.00 euro.

entries.name: Musei Capitolini Centrale Montemartini
entries.note: Roman sculpture among the turbines and diesel engines of a power station inaugurated in 1912; Tuesday to Sunday, 09:00 to 19:00.

entries.name: Sepolcreto della via Ostiense
entries.note: A burial ground used from the 1st century BC to the 4th century AD, inside Parco Schuster; booking on 060608 is obligatory, in groups of no more than 25.

entries.name: Catacomba di Commodilla
entries.note: The catacomb of Felix and Adauctus on via delle Sette Chiese, with the painting known as the Madonna di Turtura; visits are by request only.

entries.name: Gazometro di Roma
entries.note: The steel frame of the gasholder built by Ansaldo with Klonne between 1935 and 1937, 89.10 metres high, seen from via del Commercio and the Ponte della Scienza.

entries.name: Stazione di Roma Ostiense
entries.note: Roberto Narducci's travertine station of 1940, with Francesco Nagni's Bellerophon relief and black-and-white floor mosaics by Giulio Rosso and Maria Immacolata Zaffuto.

entries.name: Polo museale dei trasporti
entries.note: Rolling stock built between 1907 and 1945 in the old goods yard of the Roma-Lido terminus; closed from 2020, it reopened on 14 October 2022.

entries.name: Piazza Benedetto Brin
entries.note: Where Victor Emmanuel III laid Garbatella's first stone on 18 February 1920; the walled inscription records the date and the lots around the square date from that foundation.

entries.name: Albergo Rosso and the Alberghi Suburbani
entries.note: Innocenzo Sabbatini's transit housing of 1927-1928 on piazza Eugenio Biffi, with a canteen, a creche, laundries and shared washrooms built in.

entries.name: Teatro Palladium
entries.note: Sabbatini's cinema-theatre of 1927-28 on piazza Bartolomeo Romano, now owned and programmed by Universita Roma Tre.

entries.name: Casa del Jazz (Villa Osio)
entries.note: A villa confiscated from the Banda della Magliana and opened as a jazz venue in April 2005, with an auditorium seating about 150 in a park of 25,240 square metres.

entries.name: Porto Fluviale
entries.note: A restaurant at Via del Porto Fluviale 22, on the street that carries the Blu-painted former air force barracks at number 10.

entries.name: Ex Air Terminal Ostiense and Eataly Roma Ostiense
entries.note: The air terminal built for the 1990 World Cup beyond Stazione Ostiense, where Eataly opened its Rome store in 2012.
